name: Affogato
intro: An affogato is a scoop of vanilla ice cream 'drowned' in a shot of hot espresso. The contrast is the magic: hot, bitter coffee melting into cold, sweet cream. It's a dessert and a coffee in one, and it takes about two minutes.
heroAlt: Engraved line illustration of an affogato with espresso over ice cream

vessel.name: Small glass or dessert bowl
vessel.note: A pre-chilled glass keeps the ice cream firmer for longer.

ingredients.note: A good-quality, slightly firm vanilla works best.
Freshly pulled, from roughly 18 g of finely ground coffee.

equipment.alternative: Moka pot or AeroPress (see home methods)

steps.title: Chill the glass
steps.body: Put your glass or bowl in the freezer for 10 to 15 minutes beforehand if you can. A cold vessel slows the melting so the ice cream stays scoopable longer.
steps.tip: No time? Even a few minutes helps.

steps.title: Scoop the ice cream
steps.body: Add a round scoop of vanilla ice cream. Let it soften for a minute if rock-hard, since a slightly softer scoop is easier to shape and will melt more beautifully.

steps.title: Pull the espresso
steps.body: Pull a fresh, hot double shot of about 2 oz. Hot espresso is what creates the signature contrast, so make it just before serving.
steps.tip: A strong, slightly sweet shot balances the ice cream best.

steps.title: Pour over
steps.body: Pour the hot espresso right over the ice cream. It will melt into a creamy swirl around the scoop.
steps.tip: Serve at the table and pour in front of your guest for a little drama.

steps.title: Serve and enjoy
steps.body: Eat immediately with a spoon, since it melts fast. Each bite should have both hot coffee and cold cream.

homeMethods.note: Brew a small moka pot and pour a couple of ounces over ice cream. It's rich and bold, and works well since the ice cream softens the intensity. It won't have crema.
A concentrated AeroPress shot is a clean, strong stand-in for espresso. It's a great match for ice cream.
Use hot, double-strength coffee. It works, but it's thinner and more diluted than espresso, so the ice cream will melt faster and taste milder.

tips: Use real vanilla ice cream, since a good one makes a big difference.
Serve immediately, as it's best at the moment of pouring.
Consider a drizzle of chocolate or a sprinkle of crushed cookies on top.
commonMistakes: Letting the espresso sit and cool before pouring.
Using very soft ice cream that dissolves instantly.
Using weak coffee that disappears in the cream.

variations.name: Boozy affogato
variations.description: Add a splash of amaretto or coffee liqueur. If you do, note that this adds alcohol, so the standard coaster recipe is alcohol-free.

variations.name: Chocolate affogato
variations.description: Use chocolate or coffee ice cream for a richer dessert.

variations.name: Gelato affogato
variations.description: Vanilla gelato (fior di latte) gives a denser, silkier texture.

history: 'Affogato' means 'drowned' in Italian. It's a classic Italian dessert, though its precise origin is not well documented.

seo.title: How to Make an Affogato: Vanilla Ice Cream and Hot Espresso
seo.description: Make a classic affogato with 1 scoop of vanilla ice cream and 2 oz of hot espresso. Includes tips and no-machine alternatives.
